name: Speech representation learning

conventions.text: Start from the actual audio: show the input as a real spectrogram raster (in a colormap) or a waveform raster, not as an icon or a labelled box.
Show masking on the input itself: blank out spans of the spectrogram or waveform with flat grey.
Let only the masked positions send arrows to the prediction targets or the loss; unmasked positions get none, so the objective reads from which columns are wired.
Draw frame or text tokens as a row of small equal cells, filled by token type (masked vs visible; special, text and timestamp tokens).
Build the model as a bottom-up stack: the input enters at the base and the layers rise above it.
Draw training signals (target prediction, loss, teacher update) as dashed lines and keep the data flow as solid arrows.
Mark the input-preparation step (masking, feeding the data in) with a wide hollow block arrow; thin line arrows carry everything else.
Draw a Transformer as a plain container holding a few thin outlined bars for its layers or sublayers, not as a single solid box.
Gather a group of layers with a curly brace and attach the label, or the arrow that targets them, to the brace.

source: summarised from the evidence cards listed under each convention
